text: The system has produced a "No Tumour" output, which simply indicates that no features matching the three tumour types it was trained on were identified, not that the scan is normal [neurasight-system]. Because the model only knows four categories, any abnormality outside glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumour or the trained "no-tumour" examples - such as infarct, haemorrhage, infection or other non-neoplastic disease - may be forced into the "No Tumour" class [nci-cns-pdq-patient]. In addition, a single 2D slice does not represent the whole study, so a lesion outside the imaged plane could be missed [nci-cns-pdq-patient]. Consequently, the absence of a detected tumour does not equal the absence of disease, and clinical correlation remains essential [nci-cns-pdq-patient]. If any concerning symptoms are present, such as sudden severe headache, new seizures, loss of consciousness, weakness, visual change, confusion or persistent vomiting, urgent medical assessment is still warranted [ninds-brain-tumors]. It would be appropriate to discuss with a qualified clinician the need for a full neurological examination, formal radiological reporting of the complete study and possibly further or repeat imaging, as well as investigation of non-tumour causes and specialist referral if symptoms persist or progress [nci-cns-pdq-patient] [ninds-brain-tumors].
